title: PV-Assisted Solar Thermal Dehydrator
summary: CFD-optimized off-grid solar thermal dehydrator for rural agricultural food preservation; awarded grant funding by Energy Saving Trust & IKEA Foundation.
caption: CFD airflow and temperature distribution model for the solar thermal dehydrator chamber.
objectives: Develop an off-grid solar thermal dehydrator tailored for rural agricultural food preservation.
Optimize internal drying chamber temperature distribution and air velocity using computational fluid dynamics (CFD).
Implement PV-assisted active ventilation for uniform crop moisture removal and energy autonomy.
methods: Constructed 3D multiphysics CFD simulations to model convective heat transfer and air velocity profiles.
Integrated solar thermal collectors with auxiliary PV-powered airflow fans for off-grid operation.
Conducted experimental dehydration trials to validate thermal efficiency and drying kinetics.
resultNotes: Awarded grant funding under the Efficiency for Access Design Challenge UK (2024–2025) funded by the IKEA Foundation.

title: Two-Wheeled Self-Balancing Robot
summary: Inverted-pendulum robotics platform with real-time PID feedback control and inertial sensor fusion for dynamic equilibrium.
caption: Hardware chassis, sensor integration, and motor driver circuitry for the two-wheeled self-balancing robot.
objectives: Design an inverted-pendulum two-wheeled mobile robot with dynamic tilt stabilization.
Implement real-time PID feedback control for attitude correction under external disturbances.
Develop motor driver circuits and power management for responsive torque control.
methods: Integrated an IMU (gyroscope and accelerometer) with complementary filtering for accurate tilt angle estimation.
Programmed discrete PID closed-loop control algorithms for dynamic balance and forward/reverse motion.
Tuned proportional, integral, and derivative gains experimentally on custom motor driver hardware.
resultNotes: Maintained balance across varied surfaces and responded dynamically to push disturbances.

title: 310V / 19V 500W Dual-Stage Buck Converter
summary: High-efficiency MOSFET-based DC-DC step-down converter with symmetrical duty cycle operating at 20 kHz.
caption: Circuit schematic, switching waveforms, and voltage regulation response simulated in PSIM and MATLAB.
objectives: Design a 310 V to 19 V DC-DC step-down converter delivering up to 500 W output power.
Achieve high conversion efficiency with symmetrical duty cycles operating at 20 kHz.
Ensure strict voltage regulation and stability under varying resistive load conditions.
methods: Formulated analytical state-space equations for dual-stage MOSFET power stage switching.
Simulated inductor ripple current, capacitor voltage ripple, and thermal losses.
Evaluated dynamic load response and efficiency curves across variable resistive loading.
resultNotes: Verified stable voltage regulation across full load transitions with low output voltage ripple.
